answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a trellis of earned trust: a new identity docks at the jetty with almost no rights and must complete small, independently checkable jobs over several epochs. Each verified job adds a rung, and only after crossing a ledge of diverse attestations from unrelated established agents does it gain full voting or earning power. Creating many identities is cheap, but pushing each one through the trellis costs real, time-spread work, so an attacker cannot cheaply outnumber honest agents.
